purpose: Level 4 (Troubleshoot) of the Equity Uprise Server Lab: injected hardware faults on the sandbox clone of B1-SRV-HYP-01-I001, run on the Step 3 guided-scenario runtime. Symptoms are rendered from production/electronics/server-lab-hardware-v1.json failure modes.

safety_rules.when: a replace of a non-hot-swap part (DIMM, CPU, CMOS battery, OCP NIC) is attempted while the host is powered
a drive other than the failed member is pulled from a degraded RAID 5 array
the only healthy PSU is pulled while the host runs

scenarios.title: Server Memory Failure
scenarios.learner_ticket: The virtualization host in MDF rack 01 is up, but the hypervisor says it has less memory than yesterday and the health light is amber.
scenarios.learner_brief: Find the failed memory module from the evidence, replace it safely and prove the host has all its memory back.

dimm_uncorrectable_error.component_led: DIMM fault LED beside the slot lit amber (visible with the lid open)
post: Memory error: uncorrectable ECC on CPU1 DIMM C1; DIMM disabled
bmc_sel: Memory: Uncorrectable ECC detected on CPU1 DIMM C1
Memory: CPU1 DIMM C1 disabled at POST
dimm_uncorrectable_error.beep_or_code: POST memory warning prompt (press a key to continue)
os: Total memory 224 GB instead of 256 GB
dimm_uncorrectable_error.fix: Power off, unplug, replace the DIMM in CPU1 DIMM C1 with an identical module.
dimm_uncorrectable_error.verify: POST reports 256 GB with no memory errors; event cleared.

objectives.description: Diagnose from LEDs, the event log and the boot capture.
Power down safely and replace the failed DIMM.

observation.simulated_signal: Health LED amber · DIMM fault LED beside the slot lit amber (visible with the lid open)

ui.label: Read the management controller event log (SEL)

observation.simulated_signal: Memory: Uncorrectable ECC detected on CPU1 DIMM C1 · Memory: CPU1 DIMM C1 disabled at POST

ui.label: Read the boot (POST) capture and the host's own report

observation.simulated_signal: Memory error: uncorrectable ECC on CPU1 DIMM C1; DIMM disabled · Memory detected: 224 GB of 256 GB · Total memory 224 GB instead of 256 GB · Hypervisor reports reduced host capacity

ui.label: Shut down, unplug both PSUs, ground yourself

observation.simulated_change: Host drained of VMs, shut down and unplugged; ESD strap on.
Power off, unplug, replace the DIMM in CPU1 DIMM C1 with an identical module.
Host powered on and POST ran.

observation.validation: POST reports 256 GB with no memory errors; event cleared.

scenarios.title: Degraded RAID Member
scenarios.learner_ticket: Storage alerts say the host's data array is degraded. Virtual machines are still running, slower than usual.
scenarios.learner_brief: Identify the failed drive, hot-swap only that drive, and watch the array rebuild. Pulling a healthy member from a degraded RAID 5 destroys the volume.

raid_member_failed.component_led: Drive bay 2 status LED amber (others green, activity flashing)
bmc_sel: Drive Slot: Drive bay 2 Drive fault
os: Higher I/O latency; controller reports 1 failed physical disk
raid_member_failed.fix: Identify the failed bay (blue locate if unsure), hot-swap only that drive with an identical model; the controller starts the rebuild.
raid_member_failed.verify: Rebuild completes; virtual disk 0 back to Optimal.

observation.simulated_signal: Health LED amber · Drive bay 2 status LED amber (others green, activity flashing)

ui.label: Read the management controller event log (SEL)

observation.simulated_signal: Drive Slot: Drive bay 2 Drive fault · Storage: Virtual disk 0 degraded

ui.label: Read the boot (POST) capture and the host's own report

observation.simulated_signal: Volume online but degraded · Higher I/O latency; controller reports 1 failed physical disk

observation.simulated_change: Identify the failed bay (blue locate if unsure), hot-swap only that drive with an identical model; the controller starts the rebuild.

observation.validation: Rebuild completes; virtual disk 0 back to Optimal.

scenarios.title: Server PSU Failure
scenarios.learner_ticket: Monitoring raised 'power redundancy lost' on the virtualization host. Nothing is down yet.
scenarios.learner_brief: Prove whether the feed or the power supply failed, restore 1+1 redundancy without an outage, and confirm it.

psu_failed.component_led: PSU2 status LED amber (or off); the other PSU green
os: No outage; management alert only. The server now depends on one feed.
psu_failed.fix: Confirm the cord and the B-feed PDU outlet are live, then hot-swap PSU2.
psu_failed.verify: Both PSU LEDs green; management controller logs redundancy regained.

objectives.description: Separate a dead feed from a dead power supply.

observation.simulated_signal: Health LED amber · PSU2 status LED amber (or off); the other PSU green

ui.label: Read the management controller event log (SEL)

observation.simulated_signal: Power Supply: PSU2 Failure detected · Power Supply: Redundancy lost
PDU B outlet 07: voltage present, 0.0 A drawn. The feed is live; the load behind it is not drawing power.

observation.simulated_change: Confirm the cord and the B-feed PDU outlet are live, then hot-swap PSU2.

observation.validation: Both PSU LEDs green; management controller logs redundancy regained.

scenarios.title: Server Fan Failure / Thermal Throttle
scenarios.learner_ticket: Batch jobs on the virtualization host are running slow and the rack is louder than usual.
scenarios.learner_brief: Connect the slowdown to the hardware, replace the failed part inside the hot-swap window and verify temperatures and clocks.

fan_failed.component_led: Fan 3 fault LED amber; rotor stopped
bmc_sel: Fan: Fan 3 RPM lower critical going low (0 RPM)
Temperature: CPU1 Temp upper non-critical going high
fan_failed.fix: Hot-swap Fan 3 with the lid open, within the service window.
fan_failed.verify: All fans report RPM in range; CPU temperature and clock speed back to normal.

observation.simulated_signal: Health LED amber · Fan 3 fault LED amber; rotor stopped

ui.label: Read the management controller event log (SEL)

observation.simulated_signal: Fan: Fan 3 RPM lower critical going low (0 RPM) · Fan: Redundancy lost · Temperature: CPU1 Temp upper non-critical going high

ui.label: Read the boot (POST) capture and the host's own report

observation.simulated_signal: CPU frequency throttled (thermal) under load · Remaining fans at high speed

observation.simulated_change: Hot-swap Fan 3 with the lid open, within the service window.

observation.validation: All fans report RPM in range; CPU temperature and clock speed back to normal.

scenarios.title: Server NIC Link Down
scenarios.learner_ticket: The hypervisor warns that the host's network bond has lost a member. Services are still reachable.
scenarios.learner_brief: Work up the physical layer from the server port to the switch, fix the cheapest likely cause first and verify both links.

server_nic_link_down.component_led: NIC port 1 link LED off; the other port green
os: Hosted services still reachable on the surviving path
server_nic_link_down.fix: Check the switch-side port and the DAC; reseat or replace the cable on NIC port 1. Do not replace the NIC until the cable is ruled out.
server_nic_link_down.verify: Both links up at 10 Gb/s; bond healthy on both members.

observation.simulated_signal: NIC port 1 link LED off; the other port green

ui.label: Read the management controller event log (SEL)

observation.simulated_signal: Network: NIC port 1 link down

ui.label: Read the boot (POST) capture and the host's own report

observation.simulated_signal: Bond degraded: one member down · Hosted services still reachable on the surviving path
Core switch 1, SFP+-IN-03: administratively up, no signal from the server side. Core switch 2, SFP+-IN-03: up, 10 Gb/s.

observation.simulated_change: Check the switch-side port and the DAC; reseat or replace the cable on NIC port 1. Do not replace the NIC until the cable is ruled out.

observation.validation: Both links up at 10 Gb/s; bond healthy on both members.

scenarios.title: CMOS Battery / Clock Drift
scenarios.learner_ticket: After last night's power work the host came back with sign-in failures and certificate errors, and it stopped at a firmware prompt.
scenarios.learner_brief: Trace the errors to their hardware cause, replace the part with the host off, then restore settings and time.

front_panel: Health LED amber after a power loss
bmc_sel: Battery: System board CMOS battery low
cmos_battery_depleted.beep_or_code: POST stops at a firmware setup prompt
os: Clock wrong by years: TLS certificate validation fails
Directory sign-in fails (clock skew over 5 minutes)
Time service on this host reports a huge offset
cmos_battery_depleted.fix: Power off, unplug, replace the CR2032, restore firmware settings (UEFI boot, virtualization on), set time and resync NTP.
cmos_battery_depleted.verify: Time within a second of the NTP source; settings persist across a power cycle.

objectives.description: Connect the clock to the errors.
Replace the battery and restore time.

observation.simulated_signal: Battery: System board CMOS battery low

ui.label: Read the boot (POST) capture and the host's own report

observation.simulated_signal: CMOS checksum error: defaults loaded · System time 2000-01-01 00:00 · Clock wrong by years: TLS certificate validation fails · Directory sign-in fails (clock skew over 5 minutes) · Time service on this host reports a huge offset

ui.label: Shut down, unplug both PSUs, ground yourself

observation.simulated_change: Host drained of VMs, shut down and unplugged; ESD strap on.
Power off, unplug, replace the CR2032, restore firmware settings (UEFI boot, virtualization on), set time and resync NTP.
Host powered on and POST ran.

ui.label: Restore firmware settings and resync time

observation.simulated_change: UEFI boot and virtualization re-enabled; clock set and NTP resynchronized.

observation.validation: Time within a second of the NTP source; settings persist across a power cycle.

scenarios.title: Server Firmware Baseline Mismatch
scenarios.learner_ticket: Cluster validation flags host 1 after its RAID controller was replaced last week. Storage on that host runs in a degraded driver mode.
scenarios.learner_brief: Find what is out of baseline, plan the maintenance so no VM goes down, and apply updates in the order their dependencies need.

bmc_sel: Firmware: Inventory mismatch: BIOS 2.3.1, controller 51.20 vs baseline BIOS 2.4.0, controller 52.26
Storage: Controller firmware version not supported by installed driver
os: Storage driver loads in degraded mode; cluster validation flags the host
firmware_mismatch.fix: Apply the baseline bundle in dependency order: management controller, then BIOS, then RAID controller, then NIC.
firmware_mismatch.verify: Inventory matches the baseline; cluster validation passes.

scenarios.learner_brief: Find every fault, then fix them in the safe order: a RAID rebuild stresses every drive, so restore power redundancy before you start one.
